history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. The Sumi Baptist Church, Zunheboto (SBCZ) is a Baptist church in Zunheboto, Nagaland, affiliated with the Nagaland Baptist Church Council, and is considered one of the largest church buildings in Asia, seating about 8,500 people. The congregation was founded in 1942; construction of the present building began on 5 May 2007 (some sources say the foundation stone was laid on 7 May 2007), employed more than 2,000 workers issued Inner Line Permits, took 10 years, and cost a reported Rs 36 crore. It was completed on 31 March 2017 and dedicated on 22 April 2017 by Rev. Dr. Solomon Rongpi, General Secretary of the Council of Baptist Churches in North-East India. The building measures 203 ft in length, 153 ft in breadth and 166 ft in height (about 8 storeys), with a blue dome and white turrets, 27 rooms, and a 500 kg bell imported from Poland costing Rs 15 lakh. It was designed by architect Honoholi K. Chishi-Zhimomi. Possible duplicate: the CSV also lists 'Zunheboto Town Sumi Baptist Church' (seq 754) as a separate map listing about 1 km away; a 2017 news report called this 'the only Baptist Church in the town', so the two records may refer to the same congregation - flag for deduplication review.

town_description: Zunheboto (also Zünhebo, 'Land of Warriors') is a town in Zunheboto district, Nagaland, at about 1,852 m elevation, with a 2011 population of 22,809. It is inhabited by the Sumi Nagas; the district is 97.3% Christian. The name comes from the zünhebo flowering shrub (Leucosceptrum) abundant on the hill tops where the town is built.
